newsitem.title: USA: U.S. power output rises 3.5 pct vs. year-ago - EEI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. power output rises 3.5 pct vs. year-ago - EEI.

text.p: The electricity deliveries in the continental U.S. totaled 68,437 gigawatt hour (GWh) for the week ended Sept 7, up 3.5 percent from the same period in 1995, the Edison Electric Institute (EEI) said Wednesday.
The amount of power supplied last week to the Mid-Atlantic region indicated the largest increase against the same period a year ago, up 8.4 percent at 8,983 GWh, EEI said.
During the same seven-day period, power production in the South Central territory indicated the largest decline, down 8.6 percent at 9,326 GWh, from the corresponding 1995 week.
The South Central includes Texas, Louisiana, western Mississippi, southeastern New Mexico and most of Arkansas and Oklahoma,
Electric output in the 48 contiguous states for the latest week dropped 2.7 percent from the previous week.
Year-to-date domestic power output totaled 2.32 million GWh, up 2.2 percent from the comparable period in 1995, EEI said.
